Read the tables of a split-half reliability result

Source: R/reliability_lsa.R
as.data.frame.lsa_reliability.Rd

as.data.frame() returns the tables of a reliability_lsa() result, which holds the split-half correlation of every random split: these correlations, one row per split, or a one-row summary of their distribution, chosen with what. For a grouped result the tables of the groups are stacked.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lsa_reliability'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  what = c("replicates", "summary"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_reliability_group'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

An lsa_reliability or lsa_reliability_group object from reliability_lsa().

row.names, optional

Not used; present for consistency with the generic.

what

"replicates" (default): one row per split. "summary": one row summarizing all splits.

...

For a grouped result, passed on to each group (use it for what); otherwise not used.

Value

A data frame.

  • what = "replicates": one row per split, with replicate and correlation; a failed replicate (a half with no transitions, or no variation to correlate) is kept as NA.

  • what = "summary": one row with weights, method, R, n_failed, mean, sd, ci_low and ci_high (2.5% and 97.5% quantiles of the finite correlations).

A grouped result gains a leading group column.

See also

reliability_lsa().

Examples

rel <- reliability_lsa(lsa(engagement), R = 20)
as.data.frame(rel) |> head()
#>   replicate correlation
#> 1         1   0.9813133
#> 2         2   0.9683861
#> 3         3   0.9885036
#> 4         4   0.9873595
#> 5         5   0.9729948
#> 6         6   0.9741100
as.data.frame(rel, what = "summary")
#>   weights  method  R n_failed      mean         sd    ci_low   ci_high
#> 1    prob pearson 20        0 0.9651927 0.03308002 0.8891692 0.9939467

g <- lsa(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",
         time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
grel <- reliability_lsa(g, R = 10)
as.data.frame(grel, what = "summary")
#>   group weights  method  R n_failed      mean          sd    ci_low   ci_high
#> 1  High    prob pearson 10        0 0.9880429 0.002878287 0.9842305 0.9924178
#> 2   Low    prob pearson 10        0 0.9861624 0.004595129 0.9775524 0.9919682
